title: Dependence of charge separation efficiency on the exciton-charge transfer offset and Gaussian disorder in organic solar cells
authors: Maik Schwuchow, Carsten Deibel, Angela Thränhardt
abstract: State-of-the-art organic solar cells increasingly rely on low-offset semiconductor blends, challenging the traditional requirement of a large energetic driving force for efficient charge separation. In these systems, the energetic offset $ΔE_{\mathrm{LE-CT}}$ between local exciton (LE) and charge-transfer (CT) states approaches the thermal energy, making exciton-CT hybridization and thermal repopulation of the exciton level critical to device performance. In this work, we directly compare a macroscopic two-state rate model with three-dimensional kinetic Monte-Carlo (kMC) simulations to investigate microscopic charge separation dynamics and the role of Gaussian energetic disorder. We demonstrate that in the absence of disorder, the analytical rate model accurately reproduces kMC predictions for the whole range of $ΔE_{\mathrm{LE-CT}}$. Specifically, the macroscopic model successfully explains horizontal shifts in the internal quantum efficiency curves that arise depending on how the energetic offset is physically realized in the constituent molecules. We show that these variations can be captured entirely through the ratio of degeneracies of the LE and CT states, respectively. Introducing Gaussian energetic disorder into the kMC simulation reveals a distinct crossover behavior depending on $ΔE_{\mathrm{LE-CT}}$. While disorder is mostly detrimental at large offsets, it can significantly boost efficiency at intermediate and low offsets. Thermalization of charge carriers within the disorder-broadened density of states creates an effective driving force allowing charge separation even at zero or negative energetic offsets.
summary: This paper analyzes charge separation in organic solar cells, showing that while traditional models predict efficiency drops at low offsets, the inclusion of Gaussian energetic disorder can actually boost performance. By allowing thermalization within the disordered energy landscape, the system generates an effective driving force, enabling efficient operation even when the intrinsic material offset is small or negative.
main_problem: The study investigates how charge separation efficiency in organic solar cells depends on the energetic offset between local exciton (LE) and charge-transfer (CT) states, particularly when significant Gaussian energetic disorder is present.
main_result: Energetic disorder can significantly boost charge separation efficiency at intermediate and low offsets by creating an effective driving force through thermalization within the disordered density of states. This allows high performance even when the intrinsic offset is zero or negative.
method: The work compares results from a macroscopic two-state rate model against detailed three-dimensional kinetic Monte-Carlo (kMC) simulations to analyze charge dynamics.
model_or_system: The system models organic solar cells using donor-acceptor blends on a 3D lattice. Dynamics involve LE generation, exciton transport, and subsequent dissociation into CT states, all influenced by the offset $\Delta E_{LE-CT}$ and Gaussian disorder ($\sigma_{dis}$).
key_observables: Internal Quantum Efficiency (IQE), steady-state populations of LE and CT states, and the average energy of the occupied CT state $\langle E_{CT} angle$.
important_parameters: Exciton-Charge Transfer Offset ($\Delta E_{LE-CT}$), Disorder Strength ($\sigma_{dis}$), Temperature ($k_B T$), and material parameters like binding energies.
main_assumptions: The rate model assumes constant rates and ignores triplets; the kMC simulations focus on singlet excitons and use specific hopping/transport equations.
figures_summary: Figures show sigmoid curves of IQE vs. offset, demonstrating how disorder causes a crossover behavior: detrimental at high offsets but beneficial at low offsets by shifting $\langle E_{CT} angle$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the rate model's agreement with kMC in the absence of disorder, then introduces Gaussian disorder into the kMC simulation to map out the efficiency dependence on both offset and disorder strength.
why_interesting: The explicit modeling of charge carrier thermalization within a disordered density of states to generate an effective driving force is highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in complex quantum materials.
